Date: Thu, 18 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: limited exception for ephemeral debug tokens & runtime snapshots (DPA redline attached)

Hi Mina,

Thanks for a great demo yesterday — the integration looks promising. We reviewed the standard DPA and have one practical blocking ask from our SRE team. For complex production issues they occasionally need short-lived, scoped access to a small subset of runtime information: ephemeral debug tokens (single-use IDs tied to a call) and sampled KV-cache snapshots for a particular request flow.

To clarify: this would be used only under incident/debug sessions, by a named engineer at HoloHealth, for root-cause analysis. We propose the following limits in the DPA redline (attached):
- retention: max 72 hours for any snapshot or token logs
- sampling: no more than 0.1% of requests, and never for endpoints marked "PHI"
- pseudonymization: immediate hashing of user-identifiers before storage
- access controls: explicit access log entries and just-in-time (JIT) approval by Redwood support 

We want to avoid pushing the entire production traffic export route into Redwood’s subprocessor list; instead this would be an exception clause allowing Redwood to surface ephemeral snapshots to HoloHealth under the constraints above. Please see the attached redline (HoloHealth_proposed_redline_DPA_v1.docx) and the impact matrix.

Two asks from our side: can Product and Security confirm feasibility and whether Redwood needs specific guardrails or vendor attestations (for subprocessor use)? Also, if there are any contract language alternatives you prefer, share a short suggestion and we can iterate.

Appreciate your help — we’re trying to avoid broad export approvals while keeping on-call debugging workable.

Best,
Alex
Alex Romero
Head of SRE, HoloHealth

Thanks for looping me in. Technical summary and suggested mitigations below. I’ll keep this high level for legal/security review and provide a short product-impact note.

Technical feasibility: feasible with engineering changes and a guarded path. We can implement a scoped export path that produces:
- single-request KV-cache snapshots (per-call state)
- a one-time ephemeral debug token that maps to a single trace and expires immediately after retrieval
- server-side pseudonymization hook to hash identifiers before persistence

Operational constraints I recommend (to be captured in the DPA addendum):
1) Retention limit: 72 hours max (automatically enforced)
2) Sampling safeguard: default sampling at 0.05% with a max allowed 0.1% and an approval workflow for higher rates tied to specific incidents
3) No training allowed: exported snapshots cannot be used to train or fine-tune models
4) Access gating: role-based access with JIT approval + audit log retained by Redwood for 12 months
5) Subprocessor usage: if we use a third-party collector (e.g., LogProbe or similar), we require SOC 2 Type II evidence and a subprocessor-specific addendum that limits retention and access.

Product impact: implementing the export path will require a sprint (est ~3 weeks of infra/product effort) and a follow-up security review. We can accelerate if HoloHealth signs an addendum that accepts customer-managed KMS keys and the limited scope above.

Suggested contract language for the redline (short):
"Notwithstanding Section X.Y, Customer may request scoped, temporary exports of runtime traces and KV snapshots for troubleshooting. Exports are limited to single-request snapshots, retained no longer than 72 hours, pseudonymized per the parties' agreed hashing scheme, and may not be used for model training. Access to exports requires documented approval and is auditable by Customer and Redwood. Any third-party processor used to collect or transfer such exports must demonstrate SOC 2 Type II and be bound by this addendum."

Next steps: Legal/Security review and confirmation of whether HoloHealth will accept customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed keys with strict logging. I can draft a product note for legal with the expected engineering scope.

—Karthik

Thanks for the context and the suggested language — this is helpful. From a security & contract perspective we are open to a narrowly scoped exception if the following conditions are explicitly included in the DPA addendum and agreed in writing by the customer:

1) Encryption and key management: all exports encrypted at-rest and in-transit. Prefer customer-managed keys (CMK). If Redwood-managed keys are used, the customer must accept documented key-rotation and audit controls.
2) Access controls & auditability: JIT approval for each export with a named approver, RBAC mapping, and an immutable access audit captured and stored by Redwood for 12 months (for auditing).
3) No training or model ingestion: explicit prohibition on using exported snapshots for model training or derivation.
4) Pseudonymization & sampling: customer to identify fields considered PI/PHI; those fields must be hashed/pseudonymized prior to persistence. Sampling cap of 0.1% enforced by Redwood; any increase requires a joint incident playbook and exec-level approval.
4b) Sensitive endpoints: exports for endpoints flagged as "PHI" or regulated data are prohibited.
5) Subprocessor attestations: if a third-party is used (LogProbe/Loghound/other), we require an executed Data Processing Addendum with that subprocessor and SOC 2 Type II evidence; we must be able to disable third-party forwarding for this exception.
6) Operational playbook: documented incident playbook including notification, retention enforcement, and deletion verification (signed-off by both parties).
7) Liability and indemnities: legal will handle exact wording, but we will require limitation on scope and standard indemnities for misuse.

If HoloHealth agrees to the above, Legal can prepare a concise addendum for signature. Mina — please confirm whether HoloHealth is willing to accept CMKs or the documented Redwood-managed KMS path. Alex — if you can share the list of fields HoloHealth considers PHI/PII, we can template the pseudonymization hook.

I will also request SOC 2 evidence from our preferred collector (if needed) and circulate redline edits to the attached docx.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
